summary: Created an SSH host certificate authority on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca), used it to sign the existing ed25519 host key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1/10.100.232.10/localhost and 10-year validity, wired it into sshd via `HostCertificate` in sshd_config, and reloaded sshd. Verified end-to-end that an SSH client trusting only the CA (via an `@cert-authority` line in known_hosts, no pinned host key, StrictHostKeyChecking=yes) connects successfully. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id and healthy sshd/cert state, rebooted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd health, the certificate configuration, and CA-trust connectivity post-restart. All temporary test keys/files were removed afterward.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline: root access, sshd active, existing host keys, boot_id
Signed /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub as a host certificate with ssh-keygen -s -h
Added HostCertificate directive to /etc/ssh/sshd_config and validated with sshd -t
Reloaded sshd and confirmed active status
Verified CA-trust-only SSH connection (no host key pinning) using a temporary test client key and @cert-authority known_hosts entry, then cleaned up
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline
Triggered a single safe reboot of node1 via backgrounded `reboot` so the ack returned first
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified sshd health, HostCertificate config, and CA-trust SSH connectivity after restart
Cleaned up all temporary test keys and known_hosts files on node1
